div.head: Rect 1.1
div.ab: [1.1] Eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne, swilce is deorhege to cyniges hame ⁊ scorp to friðscipe ⁊ sæweard ⁊ heafodweard ⁊ fyrdweard, ælmesfeoh ⁊ cyricsceat ⁊ mænige oðere mistlice ðinge.

Et de multis terris maius landirectum exurgit ad bannum regis, sicut est deorhege ad mansionem regiam et sceorpum in hosticum et custodiam maris et capitis et pacis et elmesfeoh (id est pecunia elemosine) et ciricsceatum et alie res multimode.

eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne swilce is. deorhege to cyniges hame 7 scorp to friðscipe . 7 sæweard 7 heafodweard 7 fyrdweard . æl|mesfeoh 7 cyricsceat 7 mænige oðere mistlice ðinge.

Eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne, swilce is deorhege to cyniges hame and scorp to friðscipe and sæweard and heafodweard and fyrdweard, ælmesfeoh and cyricsceat and mænige oðere mistlice ðingc.

Auch erwächst von vielen Landgütern weitere Grundlast auf königlichen Befehl, wie [z. B.] ist Wildgehege für königliche Domäne und Ausrüstung zum Wehrschiff (Inlandflotte B) und See[küsten]wacht und [königliche] Leibwache und Landwehrwache, Almosengeld und Kirchensteuer und viele andere verschiedene Dinge.

Also from many estates further land-dues arise by the king's command, such as [e.g.] a deer-fence for the king's residence, and equipment for a warship (the home fleet, B), and coast-guard and [royal] bodyguard and army-guard, alms-money and church-scot, and many other various things.

Also, on many estates more land-right is originated at the king’s command such as, [to maintain] the animal-hedge for the king’s estate, and [to supply] equipment for a defence ship, and to guard the coast, and [to be a] head-guard and [to perform] military watch, [to give] alms money and church tribute and many other diverse things.

Furthermore, on many estates additional property obligations arise out of the king’s command, such as maintaining the animal hedge for the royal estate, provisioning a ship for defense, service in the coastguard, the royal guard, and the military watch, and the rendering of alms, Church dues, and many other various things.
div.note: The Quadripartitus read ‘landgerihte’. Leo corrected ‘friðscipe’ to ‘fyrdscipe’ after the Quadripartitus, which reads ‘frið’ for ‘fyrd’ five words later.

Hinter dem freiesten Grundbesitzrecht folgt das mehr belastete Herrschaftsgut, wahrscheinlich auch noch dieses vom Verf. als Bocland gedacht. (Anderer Meinung Maitland Domesday 240.) Die Verschiedenheit der Grundbesitzrechte betont Verf. des öfteren

After the freest right of landholding there follows the more heavily burdened lordship estate, which the author probably also still thinks of as bookland. (Maitland Domesday 240 takes a different view.) The author repeatedly stresses the diversity of rights of landholding
Nicht ‘dem Banne’ (Leo), to ist noch nicht Dativzeichen, sondern bed. ‘gemäss, nach’; s. Wb to A I 14; Toller 991a 5j
Not ‘to the ban’ (Leo); to is not yet a mark of the dative, but means ‘in accordance with, according to’; see Wb to A I 14; Toller 991a 5j
Vgl. Gl Jagd 6
Cf. Gl Jagd 6

Da gescirpla ‘Kleidung’, gescerpan ‘kleiden’, sceorp ‘Anzug’ heisst, versteht ‘apparel for those on board’ Toller 829b: wohl zu eng, denn gescerpan bed. auch ‘mit Waffen ausrüsten’
Since gescirpla means ‘clothing’, gescerpan ‘to clothe’, sceorp ‘garment’, Toller 829b understands ‘apparel for those on board’: probably too narrow, for gescerpan also means ‘to equip with weapons’

B verstand scipe richtig, Q vielleicht als -scipe ‘-schaft’. Auch Schmid, Andrews, Maitland bessern fyrdscip, das auch Atr kennt; s. Wb. Jedenfalls passt ‘Frieden’ (Toller, Sweet) nicht; denn der Gegensatz der Composita friðburg, friðman zu unfriðland, unfriðman, unfriðscip [s. Wb], d. h. des Inlandfriedens zu feindlichem Auslande, kann hier nicht gemeint sein

B understood scipe correctly, Q perhaps as -scipe ‘-ship’. Schmid, Andrews and Maitland, too, emend to fyrdscip, which Atr also knows; see Wb. At any rate ‘peace’ (Toller, Sweet) does not fit; for the contrast between the compounds friðburg, friðman and unfriðland, unfriðman, unfriðscip [see Wb], i.e. between the peace at home and the hostile land abroad, cannot be meant here
Vgl. Gl Schiff 6c. d
Cf. Gl Schiff 6c. d

Nicht ‘Landbewachung’ (Leo) oder ‘Hauptwacht’ (Schmid). Dass hier der König gemeint ist, ergibt nur der Zusammenhang; unten 2 heisst die Wache des Vollbauern für den Gutsherrn ebenso. Vgl. Gl Wache 1a

Not ‘guarding of the land’ (Leo) or ‘chief watch’ (Schmid). That the king is meant here emerges only from the context; below, 2, the guard kept by the full peasant for the lord of the manor is called the same. Cf. Gl Wache 1a
‘Bewachung des Lagers’ Leo; eher der Mannschaft im Ggs. zum Führer
‘guarding of the camp’ Leo; rather of the men, as opposed to the leader
